narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

A high of 30°C / 86°F is expected with a low of 19°C / 66°F. Thunder possible from midday, peaking this evening. The sky remains mostly cloudy early, mostly cloudy at midday, and mostly cloudy into the evening. Isolated Evening Showers & Thunderstorms are expected, bringing 1.8 mm of rain with a 74% chance, onset between 18:00 – 21:00. Winds will be north-northeasterly overnight, turning south-southwest by midday, with peak gusts up to 34 km/h (18 kt). The UV peak index will reach 9.3 today. Air quality reaches AQI 57 at Kisumu Airport.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Wednesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Monday will be mostly clear with three of four models wet, thunder likely, highs of 29–30 °C, and a low of 19 °C. Tuesday brings partly cloudy skies with three of four models wet and thunder likely. On Wednesday, skies are partly cloudy with four of four models wet, thunder likely, a 100% rain call, highs of 30–31 °C, and a low of 19 °C. Thursday stays mostly cloudy with four of four models wet. Friday is mostly cloudy with two of four models wet. Saturday is mostly cloudy with three of three models wet. Sunday will be mostly cloudy with two of two models wet and a 100% rain call. ECMWF holds the best rain record at Day+3 and Day+7.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values indicate thunder today, reaching 3070 J/kg for Best Match, 2380 J/kg for UKMO, 2210 J/kg for ECMWF, 1500 J/kg for ICON, and 1150 J/kg for GFS, with all five models above the thunderstorm threshold and peaking at 22:00. Any thunderstorm brings the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind. No warning is available from the national meteorological service.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Winds over Winam Gulf will run overnight at 5 km/h (3 kt) gusting 7 km/h (4 kt), then south-southwesterly by midday at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 18 km/h (10 kt), then into the evening at 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 15 km/h (8 kt); peak gust 26 km/h (14 kt). Where thunderstorms are possible, expect the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1009 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1016 hPa) — a 7 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days. Pressure is also falling toward the east, northeast, northwest, south, southwest, west — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is falling. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across 5 points, today's mean sea-level pressure sits between 1014.0 and 1016.4 hPa; falling by 1.5 hPa over three days. Pressure trend overhead shows -1.4 hPa with lowest pressure toward the north.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others overall, though ECMWF holds the best rain record at 83% accuracy across recent checks. Best Match, ECMWF, and ICON tend to under-forecast daytime highs, while GFS over-forecasts highs and under-detects thunderstorms. ECMWF, GFS, and Best Match systematically under-forecast peak winds. For today's call, daytime high of 30°C aligns with ICON and UKMO, whereas ECMWF sits lower at 28.5°C on the wrong side of its tendency to under-forecast highs. Peak gust call of 34 km/h exceeds all models, where GFS sits lowest at 16.2 km/h. Call rainfall of 1.8 mm matches UKMO's total, sitting between ECMWF's 1.2 mm and GFS's 4.1 mm. No bulletin was received from the Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD). Data sufficiency is settled with 60 checks for the least-covered model at Day+0.
